title: Disability Compensation Award Structure: One Award per Veteran
content:
**Rule.** A veteran holds at most 1 Disability Compensation award. Every service-connected disability, whenever it is granted, is rated on that single award, and the new combined rating replaces the earlier one through a rating update on the same award rather than through a second award.

**When a new award is established.** A new award is established only when the veteran holds no award whose status is authorized, running or suspended. The test is made against the compensation award records held for that veteran before the award is established; what a caller says about earlier awards does not replace those records.

| Veteran's existing award status | New grant of compensation is booked as |
|---|---|
| Authorized | A rating update on the existing award |
| Running | A rating update on the existing award |
| Suspended | A rating update on the existing award |
| Terminated (for example after renunciation or an election of pension) | A new award |
| No award on record | A new award |

**Survivors.** Survivors never hold a Disability Compensation award in their own name; survivor benefits are Dependency and Indemnity Compensation.

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A veteran whose award is running at Disability Compensation (30% Combined Rating) is granted service connection for a further condition and the combined rating becomes 50 percent. The grant is booked as a rating update on the running award, which then carries Disability Compensation (50% Combined Rating); no second award is opened. Had the earlier award been terminated after an election of pension, the grant would be booked on a new award.
